newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors sift evidence on Kim's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors sift evidence on Kim's son.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Saturday they were sifting through a mountain of papers seized in a probe into rumours that President Kim Young-sam's son took a 200 billion won ($226 million) kickback.
Prosecutors are probing rumours that Hyun-chul took 200 billion won from the businessman, acting as an agent for failed Hanbo Steel Co.
An opposition politician, who first levelled the charges, has said the money took the form of a rebate on imported German machinery.
The documents were confiscated in a police raid on Friday on the home and offices of a businessman, identified by local media as an associate of the president's second son, Kim Hyun-chul.
"As the volume of documents is huge, it will take a time to go through them," said a prosecution official.
Police hauled away boxes of papers and computer floppy discs from the property of businessman Park Tae-joong.
The official also said prosecutors were probing 11 accounts at 10 banks held by Park and his relatives.
Hyun-chul is now at the centre of a parliamentary probe into the steelmaker's collapse in a bribery and influence-peddling scandal.
Hanbo Steel became South Korea's biggest corporate casualty in January when it collapsed under $5.8 billion of debts.
Ten people, including a former cabinet minister and close political aides to president Kim, are also on trial for their roles in the scandal.
Prosecutors also reopened investigations into main creditor banks of the debt-striken Hanbo Group.
"Prosecutors began reviewing the results of a probe to the five banks by Office of Bank Supervision," said another prosecution official without elaborating.

The bank watchdog launched a special probe in January into the loans made by five domestic commerical banks. A month later it warned the banks for extending huge loans to Hanbo without proper credit analysis.

Parliament kicked off its investigation into funding for Hanbo and will call Kim Hyun-chul to testify. The ruling New Korea Party agreed to the inquiry after opposition parties attacked an earlier probe by prosecutors as a whitewash that failed to expose leading players.

Separately, prosecutors extended their probe into a doctor whose videotape of Hyun-chul discussing a top media appointment in his surgery has fuelled a political storm over the younger Kim's alleged meddling in state affairs.
A Seoul court on Saturday issued a warrant to search the home and offices of the doctor, Park Kyung-shik, a court official said.
Yonhap Television News said police later raided the premises looking for more videotapes, memos and diaries.

Hyun-chul issued an apology on Monday for causing trouble and anxiety and said he was ready to accept punishment if he had done wrong. His father said on television last month he felt shamed his son had been linked to the Hanbo scandal.
The younger Kim has no official posts but is dubbed by newspapers the "crown prince".
